text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Infectious diseases consultation to confirm the regimen and plan monitoring for cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis in a man who drinks heavily
  • Standard treatment: isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for eight weeks, then isoniazid and rifampin for eighteen weeks, by video-observed therapy with the health department, with pyridoxine
  • Monitoring: monthly symptom and weight check, sputum smear and culture monthly until two consecutive cultures are negative, liver tests at two weeks and monthly because of alcohol, and vision checks while on ethambutol
  • Public health: same-day report to the local health department, home isolation until noninfectious, and a contact investigation of his household, coworkers, and patients led by the health department
  • Alcohol care: brief intervention at diagnosis, a goal of no alcohol during treatment, counseling with a substance-use counselor, medication offered, AUDIT-C at each visit, and a safety review with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at every visit

resource.title: John Henry Holliday synthetic care plan
resource.description: Diagnosis and six-month treatment of drug-susceptible cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis in a 21-year-old dentist under the ATS/CDC/IDSA guideline (three sputum smears, nucleic acid amplification, culture and susceptibility, HIV and hepatitis testing, baseline liver tests and vision checks, isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for eight weeks then isoniazid and rifampin for eighteen weeks by video-observed therapy, stopping ethambutol on susceptibility results, monthly liver and symptom monitoring, release from isolation, two-month culture conversion, contact investigation, and public-health reporting), together with care for an alcohol use disorder that raises the risk of isoniazid liver injury (AUDIT, brief intervention, counseling, and a structured safety assessment with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline), and an honest account of a liver-monitoring gap.
